# Trigonometry

Sine, cosine, tangent, their inverses, and conversion between degrees and radians.

<h2 id="deg-to-rad"><code>DegToRad</code></h2>

```rux
pub func DegToRad(x: float64) -> float64
pub func DegToRad(x: float32) -> float32
```

Converts an angle from degrees to radians.
The conversion scales by the nearest `float64` to `Pi / 180`, making `DegToRad(180.0)` exactly [`Pi`](/docs/api/math/constants#pi). A signed zero
keeps its sign, infinities keep their sign, and a NaN remains a NaN.

| Overload                                   | Summary                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func DegToRad(x: float64) -> float64` | Converts an angle from degrees to radians.                        |
| `pub func DegToRad(x: float32) -> float32` | Converts an angle from degrees to radians at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Angle.rux#L12)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description      |
| ---- | --------------------- | ---------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | angle in degrees |

**Returns**: the equivalent angle in radians

<h2 id="rad-to-deg"><code>RadToDeg</code></h2>

```rux
pub func RadToDeg(x: float64) -> float64
pub func RadToDeg(x: float32) -> float32
```

Converts an angle from radians to degrees.
The conversion scales by the nearest `float64` to `180 / Pi`, making `RadToDeg(Pi)` exactly `180.0`. A signed zero
keeps its sign, infinities keep their sign, and a NaN remains a NaN.

| Overload                                   | Summary                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func RadToDeg(x: float64) -> float64` | Converts an angle from radians to degrees.                        |
| `pub func RadToDeg(x: float32) -> float32` | Converts an angle from radians to degrees at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Angle.rux#L31)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description      |
| ---- | --------------------- | ---------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | angle in radians |

**Returns**: the equivalent angle in degrees

<h2 id="arc-cos"><code>ArcCos</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ArcCos(x: float64) -> float64
pub func ArcCos(x: float32) -> float32
```

Computes the inverse cosine of `x` in radians.
The result lies in `[0, Pi]`: `1.0` maps to zero, either signed zero maps to `Pi / 2`, and `-1.0` maps to [`Pi`](/docs/api/math/constants#pi). An
input outside `[-1, 1]` returns a NaN, and a NaN remains a NaN.

| Overload                                 | Summary                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func ArcCos(x: float64) -> float64` | Computes the inverse cosine of `x` in radians.                        |
| `pub func ArcCos(x: float32) -> float32` | Computes the inverse cosine of `x` in radians at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/ArcCos.rux#L14)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description            |
| ---- | --------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | cosine value to invert |

**Returns**: the angle in radians whose cosine is `x`, or a NaN when `x` is outside the function's domain

<h2 id="arc-cot"><code>ArcCot</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ArcCot(x: float64) -> float64
pub func ArcCot(x: float32) -> float32
```

Computes the inverse cotangent of `x` in radians.
The result lies in `[0, Pi]`: positive infinity maps to zero, either signed zero maps to `Pi / 2`, and negative
infinity maps to [`Pi`](/docs/api/math/constants#pi). A NaN remains a NaN.

| Overload                                 | Summary                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pub func ArcCot(x: float64) -> float64` | Computes the inverse cotangent of `x` in radians.                        |
| `pub func ArcCot(x: float32) -> float32` | Computes the inverse cotangent of `x` in radians at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/ArcCot.rux#L12)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description               |
| ---- | --------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | cotangent value to invert |

**Returns**: the angle in radians whose cotangent is `x`

<h2 id="arc-sin"><code>ArcSin</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ArcSin(x: float64) -> float64
pub func ArcSin(x: float32) -> float32
```

Computes the inverse sine of `x` in radians.
The result lies in `[-Pi / 2, Pi / 2]`. A signed zero returns itself, either endpoint maps to the matching endpoint
of the result range, an input outside `[-1, 1]` returns a NaN, and a NaN remains a NaN.

| Overload                                 | Summary                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func ArcSin(x: float64) -> float64` | Computes the inverse sine of `x` in radians.                        |
| `pub func ArcSin(x: float32) -> float32` | Computes the inverse sine of `x` in radians at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/ArcSin.rux#L14)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description          |
| ---- | --------------------- | -------------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | sine value to invert |

**Returns**: the angle in radians whose sine is `x`, or a NaN when `x` is outside the function's domain

<h2 id="arc-tan"><code>ArcTan</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ArcTan(x: float64) -> float64
pub func ArcTan(x: float32) -> float32
```

Computes the inverse tangent of `x` in radians.
The result lies in `[-Pi / 2, Pi / 2]`. A signed zero returns itself, infinities approach the matching endpoint, and
a NaN remains a NaN.

| Overload                                 | Summary                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func ArcTan(x: float64) -> float64` | Computes the inverse tangent of `x` in radians.                        |
| `pub func ArcTan(x: float32) -> float32` | Computes the inverse tangent of `x` in radians at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/ArcTan.rux#L13)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description             |
| ---- | --------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | tangent value to invert |

**Returns**: the angle in radians whose tangent is `x`

<h2 id="arc-tan2"><code>ArcTan2</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ArcTan2(y: float64, x: float64) -> float64
pub func ArcTan2(y: float32, x: float32) -> float32
```

The angle from the positive x axis to the point `(x, y)`, in radians, in `(-Pi, Pi]`.
The sign of `y` decides the sign of the result, including when `y` is a zero — which is what makes the function
continuous as a point crosses the negative x axis from below, and why a signed zero matters here more than almost
anywhere else.

| Overload                                              | Summary                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func ArcTan2(y: float64, x: float64) -> float64` | The angle from the positive x axis to the point `(x, y)`, in radians, in `(-Pi, Pi]`. |
| `pub func ArcTan2(y: float32, x: float32) -> float32` | Computes the angle from the positive x axis to `(x, y)` at `float32` precision.       |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/ArcTan2.rux#L18)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description           |
| ---- | --------------------- | --------------------- |
| `y`  | `float64` / `float32` | vertical coordinate   |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | horizontal coordinate |

**Returns**: the signed angle from the positive x axis to `(x, y)`

<h2 id="cos"><code>Cos</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Cos(x: float64) -> float64
pub func Cos(x: float32) -> float32
```

Computes the cosine of `x`, where `x` is in radians.
The error is at most one ulp for every finite argument. Exact argument reduction keeps a large angle no less
accurate than a small one. Either signed zero returns `1.0`; an infinity returns a NaN, and a NaN remains a NaN.

| Overload                              | Summary                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Cos(x: float64) -> float64` | Computes the cosine of `x`, where `x` is in radians.                        |
| `pub func Cos(x: float32) -> float32` | Computes the cosine of `x` at `float32` precision, where `x` is in radians. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Cos.rux#L14)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description      |
| ---- | --------------------- | ---------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | angle in radians |

**Returns**: the cosine of `x`, in `[-1, 1]`, or a NaN when `x` is not finite

<h2 id="cotan"><code>Cotan</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Cotan(x: float64) -> float64
pub func Cotan(x: float32) -> float32
```

Computes the cotangent of `x`, where `x` is in radians.
The reciprocal is computed directly instead of as `1 / Tan(x)`, avoiding a second rounding near a pole. A signed
zero maps to an infinity with the same sign; an infinite input returns a NaN, and a NaN remains a NaN.

| Overload                                | Summary                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pub func Cotan(x: float64) -> float64` | Computes the cotangent of `x`, where `x` is in radians.                        |
| `pub func Cotan(x: float32) -> float32` | Computes the cotangent of `x` at `float32` precision, where `x` is in radians. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Cotan.rux#L14)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description      |
| ---- | --------------------- | ---------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | angle in radians |

**Returns**: the cotangent of `x`, or a NaN when `x` is not finite

<h2 id="sin-cos"><code>SinCos</code></h2>

```rux
pub func SinCos(angle: float64) -> (float64, float64)
pub func SinCos(angle: float32) -> (float32, float32)
```

Computes the sine and cosine of `angle` from one argument reduction.
Returns `(sine, cosine)`. Equivalent to calling [`Sin`](/docs/api/math/trigonometry#sin) and [`Cos`](/docs/api/math/trigonometry#cos) separately, at roughly half the cost.

| Overload                                                | Summary                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func SinCos(angle: float64) -> (float64, float64)` | Computes the sine and cosine of `angle` from one argument reduction. |
| `pub func SinCos(angle: float32) -> (float32, float32)` | Computes the sine and cosine of `angle` at `float32` precision.      |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/SinCos.rux#L21)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type                  | Description      |
| ------- | --------------------- | ---------------- |
| `angle` | `float64` / `float32` | angle in radians |

**Returns**: `(sine, cosine)` for `angle`

<h2 id="tan"><code>Tan</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Tan(x: float64) -> float64
pub func Tan(x: float32) -> float32
```

Computes the tangent of `x`, where `x` is in radians.
The error is at most one ulp for finite arguments away from poles. Exact argument reduction retains all available
information near an odd multiple of `Pi / 2`. A signed zero returns itself; an infinity returns a NaN, and a NaN
remains a NaN.

| Overload                              | Summary                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Tan(x: float64) -> float64` | Computes the tangent of `x`, where `x` is in radians.                        |
| `pub func Tan(x: float32) -> float32` | Computes the tangent of `x` at `float32` precision, where `x` is in radians. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Tan.rux#L15)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description      |
| ---- | --------------------- | ---------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | angle in radians |

**Returns**: the tangent of `x`, or a NaN when `x` is not finite
